propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang in the snapshot layer times out after 300s and raises SnapshotFetchError, which is caught and converted to a BLOCK decision with review-error reason

The voter maps the BLOCK decision to a -1 LLM-Review vote and writes a dedup row, permanently removing the change from backfill re-eligibility because reconcile only re-reviews changes with no existing vote
Infrastructure faults (timeout, connection error) should not produce durable votes; they should abstain without voting or dedup recording so the change remains eligible for backfill retry
The review bot's outer layers (app.py, reconcile.py) already implement correct no-vote-no-retry behavior for hung reviews, but the adapter layer is inconsistent and votes fail-closed on any exception
The fix distinguishes retryable infrastructure faults from genuine review conclusions via a classifier (_is_retryable_infra) and returns ABSTAIN instead of BLOCK, unblocking backfill self-healing
An abstained review must emit a VOTER_ERROR marker for observability but must POST no vote and write no dedup row
